<!-- pr-reviewer: b17b168d2d66d58a9b3011c8b0b44a70eaf680af -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge.

The review found no blocking items.

- The welded pick expands into planar strips. Each strip must pass the vertical-wall check and the existing cavity checks.
- The existing obstruction check remains active. The tests check electrode agreement, the burn verdict, duplicate picks, and stale picks.
- The decision record describes the choice and the alternatives.

I ran the build and tests locally after a clean trial merge with upstream/main at `98f093fba91aea1b63cdd1498722ca9f7d73f428`.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --no-run` | Passed |
| Motion library | 387 passed; 6 ignored; 0 failed |
| App library | 341 passed; 1 ignored; 0 failed |
| `sinker_electrode` | 8 passed |
| `sinker_electrode_body` | 6 passed |
| `sinker_electrode_mcp` | 2 passed |
| Clippy for motion and app, all targets, `-D warnings` | Passed |

This is a safety-tier review because the change affects electrode geometry. I repeated two mutations locally:

1. I restored the old app adapter. The welded-pick test in `sinker_electrode` failed with the curved-wall refusal. I restored the fix. That test and the welded-pick test in `sinker_electrode_body` passed.
2. I disabled the vertical guard in `welded_wall`. The motion test failed because it accepted the leaning strip. I restored the guard. The same test passed.

All temporary mutations were removed. No golden files changed. No UI files changed, so before/after screenshots are not required.

Requested before merge: none.

The ignored tests remain in the heavy lane. The fixtures are synthetic. This review did not exercise a CAD import or a real EDM control.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: b17b168d2d66d58a9b3011c8b0b44a70eaf680af -->

Ready for the maintainer to merge. This is an independent safety-tier review: the change reads wall geometry that feeds sinker electrodes.

Head: `b17b168d2d66d58a9b3011c8b0b44a70eaf680af`. It merges cleanly with `main` at `af83da0f4` (trial merge in a worktree, no conflicts).

What I ran (locally, on the merged tree, Windows):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib` | 387 passed; 6 ignored; 0 failed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib` | 346 passed; 1 ignored; 0 failed |
| `sinker_electrode` | 8 passed |
| `sinker_electrode_body` | 6 passed |
| `sinker_electrode_mcp` | 2 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

Law checks:

- `welded_wall` refuses an empty weld, a leaning strip and a level strip by name, and names both the welded face and the strip (`crates/motion/src/sinker_cavity.rs:223`). A stale patch id is refused with "no longer in the model: re-pick it" (`crates/app/src/operation/sinker_faces.rs:71`).
- `check_face` runs on each strip before the lean test. It refuses a non-finite normal and a non-unit normal first, so no NaN reaches the `asin` angle (`crates/motion/src/sinker_cavity.rs:95`). Index math uses `.get()` paths and lengths that `check_face` holds at three or more.
- No `unwrap()`, `expect()` or `panic!()` on a production path in the diff. The new expect and panic lines are in tests.
- The per-strip read reuses the planar-face path whole, with its existing refusals. The added pick-rule call is a no-op for face and patch ids, as before.
- Placement is right: the new rule lives in `camcraft-motion`; the app file only reads the world. Layering holds.
- No new command and no new parameter, so no MCP surface is owed; the command's existing MCP tool passes.
- No golden, snapshot PNG, UI, process, `build.rs`, scripts, workflow or dependency change. The PR touches six files.
- The body carries a `Changelog:` line and ends with the reference that closes issue 1808. Issue 1808 is open, `in-review`, `effort:high`. The commit subject is conventional.
- `docs/decisions/1808-welded-walls.md` matches the decisions format. The provenance line in the `sinker_cavity` header now names the welded-wall rule.

Notes (not blocking):

1. A production code path no longer sets `curved: true`; the patch pick expands instead. The curved-wall refusal stays pinned by the fuzz and unit tests. Keeping the field is fine.
2. A welded face picked beside its own strips counts the duplicate walls in `Cavity::walls`. The decision record states this. Nothing outside the unit tests reads the count.
3. The app lib now reports 346 passed on this merged tree; the body's 341 was on an earlier base. Nothing failed.

The fixtures are synthetic meshes. A CAD-import weld and a real EDM control were not exercised, as the body states.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
